subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on Food Preparation and Cooking Techniques, then mark my answer against the Edexcel spec.
promptWeak: Explain Food Preparation and Cooking Techniques for GCSE Edexcel Food Preparation & Nutrition simply, with an example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: Which knife grip is recommended to keep fingers safe when slicing vegetables?
options: The claw grip, with fingertips tucked under
Flat fingers pressing down on the food
Holding the food loosely in the air
questions.explain: The claw grip curls the fingertips under and out of the way while the knuckles guide the blade, protecting fingers during slicing.

questions.q: Why should knives always be kept sharp?
options: It has no effect on safety
A sharp knife needs less force and is less likely to slip
questions.explain: Sharp knives cut cleanly with less force, so they are less likely to slip and cause accidents than blunt ones, which need more pressure.

questions.q: The knife cut that produces small, even cube shapes is called:
questions.explain: Dicing cuts food into small, even cubes. Julienne is thin matchsticks and chiffonade is finely shredded leaves; even cuts help food cook evenly.

questions.q: Why is it important to cut vegetables into even-sized pieces before cooking?
options: So they all cook in the same time
questions.explain: Even-sized pieces cook at the same rate, so nothing is overcooked or undercooked, giving a consistent texture and even results.

questions.q: Why is accurate weighing of ingredients important in baking?
options: The right ratios are needed for the correct texture and rise
questions.explain: Baking is a precise science; accurate weighing keeps the ratio of flour, fat, sugar and raising agent correct so the product has the right texture and rise.

questions.q: A recipe serves 4 but you need to serve 8. What should you do to the ingredient amounts?
questions.explain: To serve twice as many people, all ingredient quantities are doubled to keep the recipe in proportion.

questions.q: At what temperature does water boil at sea level?
questions.explain: Water boils at 100 degrees C at sea level. Simmering is gentler, just below boiling, at around 85-95 degrees C.

questions.q: Which is a disadvantage of boiling green vegetables for a long time in lots of water?
options: Water-soluble vitamins such as vitamin C are lost
questions.explain: Boiling for a long time leaches out water-soluble vitamins (B and C) and can make vegetables soggy. Steaming or brief cooking retains more nutrients.

questions.q: What is the main nutritional advantage of steaming vegetables?
options: It keeps more water-soluble vitamins than boiling
It adds a lot of fat
questions.explain: Steaming cooks food in steam above the water, so fewer water-soluble vitamins are lost than in boiling, and no fat is added.

questions.q: Steaming is often recommended for a healthy diet because it:
options: Adds no fat and preserves nutrients and colour
questions.explain: Steaming adds no fat and helps preserve nutrients, colour and texture, making it a healthy cooking method, though it does not brown food.

questions.q: Which frying method uses only a small amount of oil in a pan?
questions.explain: Shallow or stir-frying uses a small amount of oil in a pan, whereas deep-frying submerges food fully in hot oil, adding much more fat.

questions.q: Why is deep-fried food less healthy than the same food when grilled?
options: Deep-frying adds a large amount of fat and energy
questions.explain: Deep-frying makes food absorb a lot of oil, greatly increasing its fat and energy content, whereas grilling lets fat drip away, making it healthier.

questions.q: Baking and roasting cook food using:
questions.explain: Baking and roasting use dry heat in an oven. Dextrinisation and caramelisation give baked and roasted foods their browned surface and flavour.

questions.q: Why is meat sometimes rested after roasting before it is carved?
options: To let the juices redistribute so it stays moist
questions.explain: Resting roasted meat lets the juices redistribute through the meat, so it stays moist and tender when carved rather than losing juice.

questions.q: Grilling cooks food mainly by which method of heat transfer?
questions.explain: Grilling uses radiant heat (radiation) from a hot element above or below the food; it is a healthy method because excess fat can drip away.

questions.q: Which food is well suited to grilling as a healthier cooking method?
options: A chicken breast or fish fillet
questions.explain: Thin, tender pieces such as chicken breast, fish or lean chops grill well; grilling lets fat drip away, making it healthier than frying.

questions.q: To keep a meal lower in fat, which change is most effective?
options: Grill or steam instead of deep-frying
questions.explain: Grilling and steaming add little or no fat, whereas deep-frying adds a lot; switching to these methods lowers the fat and energy content of a meal.

questions.q: Which cooking method best preserves the colour, texture and vitamins of stir-fried vegetables?
questions.explain: Quick stir-frying over high heat cooks vegetables fast with little water, helping preserve colour, crunch and water-soluble vitamins.

questions.q: Which is a good technique for presenting a finished dish attractively?
options: Using garnish, colour contrast and a clean plate
questions.explain: Good presentation uses garnish, contrasting colours, sensible portions and a clean plate to make food look appealing, improving its sensory appeal.

questions.q: Adding a sprig of fresh herbs and a wedge of lemon to a fish dish mainly improves its:
questions.explain: A garnish such as herbs and lemon improves the appearance and aroma of a dish, boosting its sensory appeal and making it more appetising.
